chunk_findings.detail: The update refusal still reports only the single lease `queue_ahead` returns. `queued_globs(want, ahead.globs, cfg)` is joined into one sentence for that one `(ahead.holder, ahead.item)`, so a second queued item that overlaps a different wanted glob is dropped. Given an `update --globs` of `a.py` and `b.py` while Z is queued on `a.py` and W is queued on `b.py`, the text is `those globs (a.py) are queued behind Z ...`, and `b.py` / W never appear — the same one-conflict refusal this change is meant to stop. `test_queued_behind_refusal_names_the_glob` never calls `update --globs` and only has one queued glob, so it does not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:195

chunk_findings.detail: `queue_ahead` is still a single waiter, and the rewritten refusal only runs `queued_globs(mine, ahead.globs)` against that one lease (same shape in `reservations.py` after the `ahead is None` check). Given an update/claim whose globs are `brief.py` and `lane_views.py`, with `brief.py` queued behind `sw-cedefaults` and `lane_views.py` queued behind an earlier different waiter, the message names only `brief.py` and `sw-cedefaults` and drops `lane_views.py` and its queue place. The prior probe called this residual and out of scope; it does not fix it, and the bug requires every conflicting glob with its holder or queue place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_guard_queued.py:24

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten queued refusal still calls `WG.queue_ahead` once and formats only that single `ahead`. Given an `update --globs` whose accepted globs are `brief.py` (queued behind `sw-cedefaults`) and `lane_views.py` (queued behind a different earlier waiter), `queued_globs(want, ahead.globs, cfg)` is filtered against whichever waiter `queue_ahead` returns first. The message names only that one glob and holder and then refuses the whole update (`The globs were not changed.`), so the other conflicting glob and its queue place are still omitted. The prior probe called this residual and out of scope; the new hunk did not change the single-ahead lookup, so the stated requirement to list every conflicting glob is still unmet on that input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:plan_retarget

chunk_findings.detail:
`clash_report` constructs strings with `p0!r` and `p1!r`, where `p0` and `p1` are globs (strings like `"brief.py"`). But in `ddflow/services/leases/claim.py` at line 271, the author writes: `named, _ids = clash_report(glob_clashes(state, cfg, it, holder, mine, now))` and then formats it as `f"{item_id} writes {named}"`. When a claim fails due to a glob clash, `clash_report` returns a string containing format parts like `'brief.py' overlaps 'brief.py' held by ...`. When combined with `claim.py`'s exception message, this prints `item_id writes 'brief.py' overlaps ...`, missing the expected introductory text or failing to correctly describe the overlapping files because `glob_clashes` unpacks `c.pair` where `c.pair` is `(mine_glob, theirs_glob)`. The function signature of `glob_clashes` returns `(c.item, c.lease, c.pair)`, but `_glob_clashes` in admission.py produces pairs from `conflicts(globs, lease.globs, shared)`, where the first element is from `mine` and the second from `theirs`. In `claim.py`, the old code was:
`f"{item_id} writes {pair[0]!r} which overlaps {pair[1]!r} held by {lease.holder} on {other_id}"`.
The new `clash_report` omits the `item_id writes` and `which` and `on {oid}` in a way that produces malformed English grammar (`'brief.py' overlaps 'brief.py' held by H on I; 'other.py' overlaps ...`), and when interpolated into `f"{item_id} writes {named}"`, it duplicates the item prefix and loses the clarity of the single-clash message.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/common.py:65

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten `update --globs` refusal still does not name holders or queue places. `queued_ahead` may collect every overlapping waiter, but the text thrown away that list and hard-codes `queued behind earlier waiters ([lease].wait_queue)`. Given an update of `a.py` and `b.py` while Z is queued on `a.py` and W on `b.py`, the caller sees `those globs (…) are queued behind earlier waiters ([lease].wait_queue)`, with no holder and a literal field path instead of each glob’s waiter — the same one-conflict opacity B-glob-refusal-names-one-conflict asked to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:198

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten queued-claim refusal drops the holder and queue place the old text named (`queued behind {ahead.holder} ({ahead.item})`). Given Z waiting on `a.py` and W waiting on `b.py`, the caller gets `{item}: those files (…) are queued behind earlier waiters ([lease].wait_queue)`, a literal field path and no waiter per glob. `queued_behind` is only `aheads[0].item`, so the second waiter is gone from the structured field as well. That fails the stated contract that a refusal list every conflicting glob with its holder or queue place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_guard_queued.py:24

chunk_findings.detail: The reservation path has the same regression. Previously the reason was `{named} is queued behind {ahead.holder} ({ahead.item})`. Now it is `those files ({queued_names}) are queued behind earlier waiters ([lease].wait_queue)`, and `Blocked` is built with only `[aheads[0].item]`. An update blocked by two earlier waiters on two globs therefore names neither waiter and records only the first blocking item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/reservations.py:158

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten `update --globs` refusal still does not name holders or queue places. `queued_ahead` may collect every overlapping waiter, but the text thrown to the caller hard-codes `queued behind earlier waiters ([lease].wait_queue)`. Given an update of `a.py` and `b.py` while Z is queued on `a.py` and W on `b.py`, the caller sees `those globs (…) are queued behind earlier waiters ([lease].wait_queue)`, with a literal field path instead of each glob’s waiter — the same one-conflict/vague refusal B-glob-refusal-names-one-conflict asked to fix. This is the earlier untriaged finding; the current hunk still contains that string.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:196

chunk_findings.detail: `test_queued_behind_refusal_names_the_glob` asserts `"a.py" in out.reason` and `QUEUER in out.reason` on the whole claim result, including the `Recorded:` trailer. The sibling tests in this same diff strip that trailer (`split("\n\nRecorded:")`) precisely because it already lists the requested globs and the waiter. Given the pre-fix refusal `those globs are queued behind agent-queuer` plus a `Recorded:` line that mentions `a.py` and `QUEUER`, every assertion here still passes, so the regression does not fail on the unfixed code and does not lock the queued-behind clause to naming the glob.
